coverage: Nine posts, February–November 2026. Compiled Sunday, Nov. 1, ET.

items.author: Stephen Penders
items.text:
A recent post by @naval made me introspective about the passage of time and its relativity to parenthood.

My son is 15. He's going to be out of the house and living his own life much sooner than I realize. I try to spend time with him as much as I can, yet there's always an excuse to occupy my attention elsewhere.

I wish I'd spent more time with him when he was younger. I look forward to spending time with the man he becomes when he's 25 and even 35.

But the present is now. And here I am pontificating on X about the whole thing instead of being with him.

I'm gonna go wake his ass up to play catch and grab some burgers. He's much more important than building a brand on social media.

quoted.author: Stephen Penders
quoted.text: @naval My son is 15, man. He was 3 years old about twenty minutes ago. Time escapes you. Grandkids are around the corner, trying not to blink.

items.author: Joe Hudson
items.text: I like to think of changing behavior the way I think of water. If you try to grab at it or mold it into something, it will slip through your fingers. But change its container, and it naturally flows into a new shape.

items.author: Steven Phillips, MD
items.text: New Hopkins study shows that a couple of doses of psilocybin provides benefits lasting 6 months in chronic Lyme patients. This is consistent with what I’ve seen in patients over the years.

items.author: Preethi Kasireddy
items.text:
There are 2 types of women with PCOS. Lean and overweight.

The overweight ones get told to lose weight (accurate). The lean ones rarely get their insulin checked.

On the gold standard test, 75% of lean women with PCOS were insulin resistant.

Being thin doesn't mean you are healthy. Ask for fasting insulin.

items.author: Naval
items.text:
You’re here because an unbroken chain of your ancestors, from tadpoles to monkeys to now, replicated. 

Don’t be the first one to miss the branch.

quoted.author: Matthew Schmitz
quoted.text: The sociologist Susan Pickard chose career over motherhood. She writes about being the last of her line.
